data.text/markdown:
🛰️ Alternative data — short interest, insider, fundamentals, ratings, price targets

The single entry point for alt-data ingestion. This repo's own providers — FINRA (short interest), SEC EDGAR (Form 4 insider trades and XBRL companyfacts fundamentals) and Yahoo Finance (analyst rating changes and price targets) — write to the shared TimescaleDB; the option chains of §5b are local files. No dependency on the sibling stock-trading repo. Every run fetches only what is missing, for every name in the database. The coverage ledger (altdata_coverage) records, per dataset and name, the window already fetched. A run fetches, name by name, the history back to BACKFILL_START that a name lacks and the days since its last refresh (re-reading a short overlap, cli._OVERLAP_DAYS, for data published late). A name refreshed recently costs nothing; one never ingested gets its whole history. Insider history up to SEC's newest quarterly data set comes from those bulk files (one download serves every company), only the days after it from the per-filing scraper. Stop a run whenever you like: every finished name is recorded at once, and the next run continues after it. §2 shows the plan before anything is downloaded; the button in §3 starts it. Point-in-time by construction: every row is stamped known_at (SEC acceptance, FINRA dissemination, the rating's announcement), so features never see a value before it was public. Writes UPSERT on natural keys, so a re-run is safe and idempotent.
Why the audits matter. A half-ingested table does not fail loudly — it goes quiet. short_interest once shipped covering 3 of 100 names and read as fresh, because the check only looked at the newest row; the strategy ranked those 3 and gave 97 a neutral 0.5. In 2026 a one-universe update left informed_flow's 500 names on weeks-old short interest with every check green, and from July 2026 short interest reached only ~765 of ~2,300 names. So this notebook now always covers the whole registry, §4 checks breadth and depth (not just recency), and §4a audits the NEWEST data of every universe a strategy trades.
Flow: parameters → what is missing → ingest → ledger → freshness, breadth & depth → per-symbol coverage → option chains → schema.
1 · Parameters
DB localhost:5432/trading · ALL: 2323 names · traded: LiquidLeaders (conviction_flow, value_factor); Liquid500 (informed_flow, informed_flow_ls, turnover_momentum)

2 · What is missing

The plan the ingest will follow, read from the ledger (nothing is downloaded here). up to date: refreshed within STALE_DAYS and complete back to BACKFILL_START. to fetch: a refresh of the days since its last run, plus — with missing history — the history it lacks (new names get everything). Re-read after every ingest: a finished run leaves every name up to date.

data.text/markdown:
3 · Ingest what is missing

Each dataset runs as one paced tsim altdata subprocess: SEC and FINRA rate-limit per IP, so — like the IBKR rule — there is no fan-out. Progress streams below the cell, one line per name ([i/n]). ratings and price_target come from the same Yahoo response; they are two tables because they are two signals (most target revisions arrive with the rating unchanged).
Ingest finished at 2026-10-20 15:31; the plan and every audit below re-read the DB.

4 · Freshness, breadth & depth

Three questions, not one. Fresh (is the newest row recent?), broad (how many of the names are present?) and deep (how far back does it go?). The old version of this check asked only the first, which is exactly how a 3-of-100-name short_interest table passed as healthy. A ⚠ means the sleeve is not safe to trade on: a ranker drops a signal covering less than half its names, but one broad enough to survive that floor yet still patchy quietly distorts the ranking. These read the whole history; §4a asks whether the newest data is broad in every universe a strategy trades.

data.text/markdown:
4a · Is the newest data broad — in every universe a strategy trades?

Breadth over the whole history cannot see a table that went stale at its end. So, for every universe in TRADED and every dataset its strategies read: the share of its names the ledger refreshed in the last FRESH_DAYS, and — short interest being scheduled — the share the newest settlement covers. A ❌ here is not safe for a live book; a backtest that ends before the gap is unaffected.

data.text/markdown:
4b · Fundamentals: is any concept frozen?

A company that keeps filing keeps its fundamentals rows arriving — even when one concept inside them stopped updating years ago. That is how the share counts of V, MA and CMCSA sat on their 2010 values. The parser now falls back tag by tag per filing, but a filer can still stop reporting a concept, so audit per concept:
  • frozen — the concept's newest row is more than MAX_AGE_DAYS behind the company's newest filing. The feature layer masks such values, so the name drops out of any ranking that needs the concept.
  • missing — the concept has no row at all for that name.

data.text/markdown:
4c · Analyst feeds: has any name's feed been cut?

A feed that stops for ONE name does not fail, it goes quiet. Yahoo's analyst list (the only source of ratings and price_target) ends in October 2024 for SMCI, CAT, META, FANG, WELL … although those names are covered as heavily as ever, and Yahoo itself returns nothing newer, so re-ingesting cannot fix it. A ranker would read two years of silence as "no analyst news". A name is flagged when its silence, up to the last time the ledger refreshed it, is at least MIN_SILENT_DAYS and would have produced at least CUT_EXPECTED actions at its own pace over the two years before its last action (zero events at that pace has probability ≈ e⁻¹⁰). An acquired or delisted name flags too; either way its data after last must be MASKED by a feature that uses it, never read as zero.

data.text/markdown:
5 · Per-symbol coverage & gaps

An average hides exactly the failure that matters: a dataset can look 80% covered while a fifth of the names have no data at all. This section goes name by name — over the names the strategies trade when the run covers more than AUDIT_MAX names. What counts as a gap depends on the dataset: short_interest is scheduled (FINRA, about twice a month), so a missing settlement really is a gap. insider, ratings and price_target are irregular event streams: a quiet stretch is not a gap, but a name with zero events over the whole window (it rides the neutral 0.5 rank forever) or a silence wildly out of line with the limit is.

data.text/markdown:
5b · Option chains (local files, not the DB)

The opt_* features (informed_flow_ls) come from MarketData.app's end-of-day option chains, which scripts/marketdata_dump.py downloads into var/marketdata/chains/ (one gzip CSV per name and month; rerun it daily). They carry no implied volatilities, so providers.marketdata.build_cache() solves them and reduces each name-day to a few numbers (ATM IV, put skew, call − put IV, volumes) in var/options/. The first build reads every file (about 5 minutes); later builds redo only the files the daily dump touched. The audit asks the same breadth question as §4a: does the NEWEST day of chains cover the names the strategies trade? A name whose chains stop is masked by the feature layer after features._OPT_MAX_AGE_DAYS days, never carried.
Press the button to build and audit the cache.

6 · Schema sanity

Each alt-data table must still have the columns the feature layer reads. They are defined in this repo's schema.sql with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (insider_trades, analyst_ratings and short_interest column-for-column identical to the sibling repo's), so this also catches drift if the sibling altered anything. A missing table: run uv run tsim init-db.
insider_trades: OK analyst_ratings: OK analyst_price_targets: OK short_interest: OK fundamentals: OK
